title: Microsoft Patches 398 Windows Flaws Including Actively Exploited WinSock Zero-Day
content_md: Microsoft has released its August 2026 Patch Tuesday security updates, addressing 398 CVEs across Windows, Office, SharePoint Server , Azure services, .NET, PowerShell, Visual Studio Code, and other enterprise products. The release includes three zero-day vulnerabilities, one of which is an elevation-of-privilege flaw in the Windows Ancillary Function Driver for WinSock that is being actively exploited in the wild. The actively exploited issue, tracked as CVE-2026-68820, affects the Windows Ancillary Function Driver for WinSock (AFD.sys), a kernel-mode component responsible for handling socket operations. Microsoft Patches 398 Windows Flaws Microsoft rates the flaw as Important, but its confirmed exploitation and potential to provide SYSTEM-level privileges make it the highest-priority remediation target in this month’s cycle. CVE-2026-68820 is a use-after-free vulnerability that an authenticated attacker can exploit locally. Successful exploitation requires code execution on a vulnerable Windows device first; however, an attacker who triggers the flaw can elevate their privileges to SYSTEM, gaining near-complete control over the endpoint. Such local privilege-escalation bugs are commonly chained with phishing, malicious documents, browser exploits, or remote-access compromises, converting an initial foothold into full administrative access.
